record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
record.context_brief: Picard-type omitted set after polynomial hull
record.original_question: Let K be a non-constant analytic multifunction on C. For each z, let K-hat(z) denote the polynomial hull of K(z), and let K-hat(C) be the union of K-hat(z) over z in C. How large can the exceptional set C \ K-hat(C) be? In particular, can this exceptional set be uncountable?

evidence.quote: We recall that K-hat denotes the polynomial hull of K, as defined in Theorem 2.7.
Problem G. Let K be a non-constant analytic multifunction on C. How large can C \ K-hat(C) be?
However, we know of no example where C \ K-hat(C) is uncountable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An analytic multifunction on $\mathbb{C}$ is an upper semicontinuous set-valued map $K$ that assigns to each $z\in\mathbb{C}$ a non-empty compact subset $K(z)\subset\mathbb{C}$, such that for every open set $U\subset\mathbb{C}$ the set $\{z:K(z)\subset U\}$ is open and such that $-\log\mathrm{dist}(\cdot,K(\cdot))$ (or, equivalently, the appropriate plurisubharmonic test) makes $K$ behave analytically; concretely, $K$ is analytic if for every open $V\subset\mathbb{C}$ and every subharmonic function $u$ on a neighborhood of the graph of $K$ over $V$, the function $z\mapsto \sup\{u(z,w):w\in K(z)\}$ is subharmonic on $V$. For a compact set $L\subset\mathbb{C}$, let $\widehat{L}$ denote its polynomial hull, namely the set of all $w\in\mathbb{C}$ for which $|p(w)|\le\sup_{\zeta\in L}|p(\zeta)|$ for every polynomial $p$ (equivalently, $\widehat{L}$ is $L$ together with the bounded components of $\mathbb{C}\setminus L$). For an analytic multifunction $K$ on $\mathbb{C}$, define $\widehat{K}(z):=\widehat{K(z)}$ and 
$$\widehat{K}(\mathbb{C}):=\bigcup_{z\in\mathbb{C}}\widehat{K}(z)\subset\mathbb{C}.$$
Assume $K$ is non-constant.

How large can the exceptional set $\mathbb{C}\setminus\widehat{K}(\mathbb{C})$ be? In particular, does there exist a non-constant analytic multifunction $K$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which $\mathbb{C}\setminus\widehat{K}(\mathbb{C})$ is uncountable?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open question in a recent survey on open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions; no example with uncountable exceptional set is known, and searches did not reveal any subsequent resolution. Related literature on polynomial hulls without analytic discs (e.g., Izzo–Levenberg) does not address this Picard-type question.

status_evidence.title: A Cantor set whose polynomial hull contains no analytic discs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial hulls strictly larger than the set but containing no analytic discs.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on polynomial hulls exist but do not resolve the uncountability question for the exceptional set of an analytic multifunction.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
status_evidence.snippet: How large can C \ K-hat(C) be? We know of no example where it is uncountable.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open with no known uncountable example.
